speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your weakness and fatigue, could you please describe when these symptoms started and if they have been getting progressively worse?

text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent travel and camping history, have you noticed any specific symptoms like fever, night sweats, or a rash that might suggest an infection? I also need to know if you have experienced any shortness of breath, palpitations, or unexplained weight loss.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the diplopia fluctuate in severity, worsening with sustained gaze or at the end of the day, and do you experience any difficulty with swallowing or speaking that also worsens with use? I will also request a CBC and a thyroid panel to check for anemia or thyroid dysfunction. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Thyroid_Function_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal blood work and your history of fluctuating diplopia and fatigue that worsens with use, are you experiencing any ptosis (drooping eyelids) or weakness in your limbs that improves with rest? I will request an acetylcholine receptor antibody test to confirm my suspicion. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results. Do you also experience difficulty with swallowing or speaking that worsens later in the day? DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
